mainTopic: Fat and mucus as seals for holes, the corrected rulings on טרפה and אבל, comparing holes (מקיפין), and a hole in the rectum
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question on רב נחמן's rule that only permitted fat (בר חמצא) seals a hole. The גמרא answers by splitting the קיבה into a curved 'bow' side and a straight 'bowstring' side. It gives two versions of which side is in dispute. It then shows how the people of ארץ ישראל ate this fat after removing a handful, with stories about רבי אמי and רבי חנינא. Next comes a ברייתא in which רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says mucus (ליחה) sealing a hole in the intestines keeps the animal כשרה. A report in the name of רבי יוחנן says the הלכה follows him on טרפה, and follows רבי שמעון on a late-arriving mourner (אבל). A scholar checks the report with רבי אבא and learns that the טרפה part was backwards. The final ruling is that the animal is a טרפה, while in אבל we follow the lenient רבי שמעון, as שמואל taught. The amud then teaches that a doubtful hole may be compared with a new hole (מקיפין) in the intestines, the lung and the windpipe, with limits on what may be compared. It closes with זעירי's rule that a hole in the חלחולת is kosher where the hips hold it, and רבא's objection to quoting this in רב נחמן's name, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Does the fat we avoid also fail to seal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge. The fat of the קיבה is eaten by בני מערבא, so can it really be that for us in בבל it also does not seal a hole?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for us, does it also not seal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question it began just before this. If the people of ארץ ישראל eat this fat, how can we say it does not seal a hole, just because we in בבל are strict about eating it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רב נחמן, only forbidden fat (חמצא) fails to seal. If בני מערבא eat this fat, it cannot be fat that the תורה forbids. So our extra strictness about eating it should not stop it from working as a seal.

keyTerms.meaning: For us, meaning the people of בבל
Seals (closes up) a hole
Also

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate questions here. One is whether you may eat the fat. The other is whether it seals a hole. Being strict about eating something does not automatically mean it fails to seal.

phrases.english: And for us, does it also not seal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge against רב נחמן's rule that began on the previous amud
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the fat of the קיבה is חמצא, which does not seal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fat that some communities eat cannot be forbidden by the תורה. So it should count as בר חמצא and seal a hole, even for the people of בבל who are strict about eating it.

steps.title: The bow side is forbidden; the dispute is only about the bowstring side
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees the fat on the curved 'bow' side of the קיבה is forbidden. The disagreement between ארץ ישראל and בבל is only about the fat on the straight 'bowstring' side.
steps.simpleTranslation: The fat on the bow: everyone agrees it is forbidden. Where they disagree is about the fat on the bowstring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by splitting the קיבה into two sides. Only one side is actually in dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fat on the curved side is forbidden by everyone, so that is the חמצא that does not seal. The fat on the straight side is the fat that בני מערבא eat. Since it is permitted, it is בר חמצא and does seal, even for the people of בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'bow', the outer curved side of the קיבה
The 'bowstring', the straight inner side of the קיבה
Everyone agrees
They disagree
Forbidden

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַקַּשְׁתָּא – כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דַּאֲסִיר,
phrases.english: Regarding the fat on the bow, everyone agrees that it is forbidden;
phrases.notes: The קיבה is shaped like a bow: one side curves, and the other side is straight like the string.

phrases.english: where they disagree is about the fat on the bowstring.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאַקַּשְׁתָּא כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דַּאֲסִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing down which fat is in dispute
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: the fat is divided into two sides of the קיבה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All the fat of the קיבה is one kind, so if בני מערבא eat it, it must seal
steps.terutzMaskana: The bow side is forbidden by all and does not seal (חמצא). The bowstring side is the disputed fat, and it does seal (בר חמצא).

steps.title: A second version: the bowstring side is permitted; the dispute is about the bow
steps.stepSummary: Another version reverses it. Everyone permits the fat on the bowstring side, and the disagreement is about the fat on the bow side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: the fat on the bowstring, everyone agrees is permitted. Where they disagree is about the fat on the bow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way the answer was reported. It switches which side of the קיבה is the one in dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the bowstring fat is permitted by all, so it is בר חמצא and seals. The disputed fat is now on the curved bow side, and that is the חמצא. The answer still works the same way: the fat that seals is a different fat from the one we are strict about.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted

phrases.english: There are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַיִּיתְרָא – כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּשְׁרֵי,
phrases.english: regarding the fat on the bowstring, everyone agrees that it is permitted;
where they disagree is about the fat on the bow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the answer in step 2, with the two sides switched
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case, in a second version
steps.terutzMaskana: The bowstring fat is permitted by all and seals (בר חמצא). The bow fat is the disputed fat (חמצא).
steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, one side of the קיבה is agreed upon and the other side is disputed. In the first version the disputed fat is on the bowstring side; in the second version it is on the bow side.

steps.title: How they ate it: first remove a handful
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how the people of ארץ ישראל ate this fat. Two sages teach that you first remove a handful of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רב אויא said in the name of רבי אמי: we remove a handful. And רבי ינאי said the same in the name of a certain elder: we remove a handful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a practical detail. When בני מערבא ate this fat, they first took off a handful and only then ate the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even those who permit this fat did not eat all of it. They first removed a portion, and the remaining fat was eaten. Two separate sages of ארץ ישראל report this same practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Like this, in the way described here
We remove a handful (from the root קמץ, a fistful)
A certain elder whose name is not given

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב אַוְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: As that which Rav Avya said in the name of Rabbi Ami:
we remove a handful,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי מִשּׁוּם זָקֵן אֶחָד:
phrases.english: and so said Rabbi Yannai in the name of a certain elder:
we remove a handful.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב אַוְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes how בני מערבא actually ate the fat discussed above
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before eating this fat, a handful is removed, and the rest is eaten.

steps.title: רב אויא saw רבי אמי eat it
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא reports what he saw himself. They removed a handful of the fat, gave רבי אמי the rest, and he ate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אויא said: I was standing before רבי אמי. They removed a handful, gave him the rest, and he ate.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא backs up the teaching with a story he saw with his own eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the rule was really followed in practice. A great sage actually ate the fat once a handful had been removed.

keyTerms.meaning: I was standing before him, meaning I saw it myself
And he ate

steps.whatToRemember: The people of ארץ ישראל really ate this fat after removing a handful, even though the people of בבל are strict about eating it.

phrases.english: Rav Avya said:
I was standing before Rabbi Ami;
they removed a handful and gave him the rest, and he ate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַוְיָא הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the teaching in step 4 with something רב אויא saw
steps.raayaObject: That the practice of removing a handful and eating the rest was really followed
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אויא saw it himself when רבי אמי ate the fat

steps.title: רבי חנינא's attendant hesitates over the fat
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא tells his attendant to remove a handful of the fat and give him the rest to eat. The attendant hesitates, so רבי חנינא tells him that as a Babylonian he should cut it all off and throw it away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא's attendant was standing in front of him. רבי חנינא said: 'Take off a handful and give me the rest to eat.' He saw the attendant hesitating and said: 'You are a Babylonian, so cut it off and throw it away.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another story showing how the people of ארץ ישראל ate this fat once a handful was removed. It also shows that a Babylonian would not eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This backs up steps 4–5: in ארץ ישראל they removed a handful and ate the rest. The attendant's hesitation shows the בבל custom was stricter. רבי חנינא does not force his own custom on him: for you, as a Babylonian, it is forbidden, so throw it all away.

keyTerms.meaning: His attendant, the student who served him
Take off a handful (of the fat)
Hesitating, holding back
A Babylonian, someone from בבל
Cut it off and throw it away

steps.whatToRemember: ארץ ישראל: remove a handful of the fat, then eat the rest. בבל: the fat is not eaten at all.

phrases.english: The attendant of Rabbi Chanina
was standing before Rabbi Chanina.
He said to him: Take off a handful,
and give me the rest so that I can eat.
He saw that he was hesitating.
He said to him: You are a Babylonian,
so cut it off and throw it away.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁמָּעֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא הֲוָה קָאֵי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story that supports the practice of removing a handful, after רב אויא's story in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That in ארץ ישראל the fat was eaten after removing a handful, while a Babylonian would avoid it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: What happened between רבי חנינא and his attendant.

steps.title: Mucus sealing a hole in the intestines
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that if the intestines have a hole but לֵיחָה seals it, the animal is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: If the intestines have a hole, and mucus seals them, the animal is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic. It quotes a ברייתא about a hole in the intestines that is sealed by mucus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a hole in the intestines makes the animal a טרפה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds an exception: if the body's own mucus closes the hole, the animal stays כשרה. The category of a dangerous hole stays the same; the seal changes the outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: The intestines
That were punctured, that have a hole
Mucus, a moist slimy substance
Seals them, closes them up
Kosher, the animal may be eaten

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Intestines that were punctured,
and mucus seals them, the animal is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the fat of the קיבה to a new case: what can seal a hole in the intestines.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intestines with a hole sealed by לֵיחָה are כשרה, according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: What is this mucus?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly the לֵיחָה in the ברייתא is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'mucus'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the word לֵיחָה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling depends on knowing which substance counts as a seal. Without a clear definition, nobody could apply it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is?

phrases.english: What is 'mucus'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of a key word in the ברייתא from step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What substance is meant by לֵיחָה.

steps.title: רב כהנא defines the mucus
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא explains that לֵיחָה is the slime of the intestines that comes out when they are pressed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: It is the slime of the intestines that comes out by pressure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the question and defines לֵיחָה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not any wetness counts. It is the thick slime of the intestines that only comes out when you squeeze or scrape them. Because it is that thick, it can really close a hole.

keyTerms.meaning: Slime, sticky mucus
Of the intestines
By means of pressure, when pressed

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: The slime of the intestines
that comes out through pressure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: לֵיחָה is the slime of the intestines that comes out under pressure.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules on טרפה and אבל
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of teachers, רבי יוחנן rules that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in טרפה and רבי שמעון in אבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The colleagues of רבי אבא learned from רבי אבא; who are they? רבי זירא. Some say the colleagues of רבי זירא learned from רבי זירא; who are they? רבי אבא. רבי אבא son of רבי חייא בר אבא said: This is what רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in טרפה, and the הלכה follows רבי שמעון in אבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first records who passed on this teaching. Then it gives רבי יוחנן's two rulings of הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two versions of who learned it from whom: רבי זירא from רבי אבא, or רבי אבא from רבי זירא. Either way, the teaching itself is the same. As reported here, it makes the ברייתא of step 7 practical הלכה, though step 16 will show this report was mistaken. It also adds a second, unrelated ruling about mourning.

keyTerms.meaning: They learned (as a received tradition)
The colleagues, the group of scholars
The practical law follows the view of
An animal with a fatal defect, which may not be eaten
Mourning

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two names. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is the one about טרפה. רבי שמעון, a different תנא, is the one about אבל.
steps.whyThisMatters: As reported here, this would make רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view on לֵיחָה the practical הלכה. But step 16 shows the report was backwards, and step 19 rules that the animal is a טרפה.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמִירִי חַבְרַיָּא דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא מֵרַבִּי אַבָּא,
phrases.english: The colleagues of Rabbi Abba learned from Rabbi Abba.
And who are they? Rabbi Zeira.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ חַבְרַיָּא דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא,
phrases.english: And some say: the colleagues of Rabbi Zeira learned from Rabbi Zeira.
And who are they? Rabbi Abba.
phrases.notes: The two versions just switch who was the teacher and who was the student.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba, son of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, said:

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בִּטְרֵפָה,
phrases.english: The halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel regarding a tereifa,
and the halacha follows Rabbi Shimon regarding mourning.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּמִירִי חַבְרַיָּא דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא מֵרַבִּי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling of הלכה on the ברייתא of step 7, and adds a ruling on mourning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in טרפה and רבי שמעון in אבל.

steps.title: Identifying the טרפה ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the טרפה ruling is the one just taught, about לֵיחָה sealing a hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל regarding טרפה': that is what we just said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to explain each half of רבי יוחנן's statement. The first half is easy: it points back to the ברייתא about mucus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added here. It simply ties the first ruling to step 7. That leaves the mourning ruling as the part that still needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what we already said

phrases.aramaic: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בִּטְרֵפָה –
phrases.english: 'The halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel regarding a tereifa':
this is what we said.
phrases.notes: Back in step 7: a hole in the intestines sealed by mucus is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בִּטְרֵפָה הָא דַּאֲמַרַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of רבי יוחנן's statement in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The טרפה ruling refers to the ברייתא about לֵיחָה.

steps.title: Which mourning ruling of רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which view of רבי שמעון about אבל רבי יוחנן means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'According to רבי שמעון regarding mourning': what is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which teaching of רבי שמעון about mourning is meant. This sets up the source it is about to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the טרפה ruling, this one has not been mentioned in the סוגיא at all. So the גמרא has to find the source where רבי שמעון rules about mourning.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? Which ruling is this?

phrases.english: 'According to Rabbi Shimon regarding mourning':
what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the second half of רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ruling of רבי שמעון about אבל רבי יוחנן means.

steps.title: A mourner who arrives in the first three days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting the source: during the first three days, a mourner who comes from a nearby place counts his mourning together with the others.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: During all of the first three days, if he comes from a nearby place, he counts with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting the source about mourning that holds רבי שמעון's view. The quote continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case: a relative joins the mourning late. If he arrives from a nearby place within the first three days, he does not start his own count. He finishes the days of mourning together with the family. רבי שמעון's own opinion comes later in the source.

keyTerms.meaning: The first three days of mourning
A nearby place
He counts together with them (finishes mourning with the family)

phrases.english: As we learned: During all of the first three days,
if he comes from a nearby place,
he counts with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering step 12 by quoting the source about mourning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source about a mourner arriving within the first three days; רבי שמעון's view follows in the continuation.

steps.title: The rest of the ברייתא about a late-arriving mourner
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. A mourner who comes from far away counts his own seven days. After the first three days, even one from nearby counts on his own. רבי שמעון says that even on the seventh day, one who comes from nearby joins the others' count.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he comes from a distant place, he counts on his own. From then on, even if he comes from a nearby place, he counts on his own. רבי שמעון says: even on the seventh day, if he comes from a nearby place, he counts with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא it began in the last step. This shows us exactly which view of רבי שמעון in אבל רבי יוחנן was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allows a nearby mourner to join the family's count only during the first three days. רבי שמעון allows it even on the seventh day. Joining their count means he finishes mourning sooner, so רבי שמעון is the more lenient view.

keyTerms.meaning: A distant place
He counts his seven mourning days on his own
From this point on (after the first three days)

phrases.english: If he comes from a distant place, he counts on his own.
From this point forward,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ בָּא מִמָּקוֹם קָרוֹב – מוֹנֶה לְעַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: even if he comes from a nearby place, he counts on his own.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ בְּיוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: Even on the seventh day,
if he comes from a nearby place, he counts with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ בְּיוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quotation begun in step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The view of רבי שמעון meant by רבי יוחנן is that a mourner from nearby joins the others' count even on the seventh day.

steps.title: A scholar travels to check the טרפה ruling firsthand
steps.stepSummary: An unnamed scholar wishes to learn the ruling from the person who said it. He goes up, finds רבי אבא son of רבי חייא בר אבא, and asks whether he really said the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone said: May I merit to go up and learn this teaching from the mouth of its master. When he went up, he found רבי אבא son of רבי חייא בר אבא and asked him: Did the master say the הלכה is like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on טרפה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. A scholar wants to check the ruling from step 10 by asking the source directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling had reached the scholar secondhand through a chain of teachers. He wants to confirm it from the one who said it, and he starts with the טרפה part.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone (a scholar whose name is not given)
May I merit to go up (to ארץ ישראל)
A teaching or ruling
From the mouth of the one who said it

phrases.english: Someone said:
May I merit to go up
and learn this teaching from the mouth of its master.
phrases.notes: "Its master" means the person the ruling was reported from, so he can hear it firsthand.

phrases.english: When he went up,
he found Rabbi Abba
son of Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba.
He said to him: Did the master say

phrases.aramaic: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בִּטְרֵפָה?
phrases.english: that the halakha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel regarding a tereifa?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיזְכֵּי וְאֶיסַּק וְאֶגְמְרַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתָּא מִפּוּמֵּיהּ דְּמָרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both halves of רבי יוחנן's ruling have been identified, the story tests whether that ruling was reported correctly
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the הלכה really follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about לֵיחָה sealing a hole

steps.title: רבי אבא: I said the opposite
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא answers that he never said the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. He said the הלכה does NOT follow him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That? I said the הלכה is not like him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא corrects the report. The ruling on טרפה was passed along backwards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The report in step 10 said the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The source says the reverse, so לֵיחָה sealing the hole does not save the animal, and it stays a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה is not like that view

steps.confusionAlert: Don't keep step 10's version of the טרפה ruling. The person it came from says it was the opposite: the animal is still a טרפה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
This? I said "the halakha is not" like him.
phrases.notes: Literally "this, 'there is no הלכה,' I said." He is flipping the report around.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הלכה is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on טרפה.

steps.title: What about רבי שמעון in mourning?
steps.stepSummary: The scholar asks about the second half of the report: is the הלכה like רבי שמעון regarding אבל?
steps.simpleTranslation: Like רבי שמעון regarding a mourner, what is the ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: The scholar now checks the second half of the reported ruling, the part about mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the טרפה half turned out to be reported backwards, he wants to know whether the אבל half is accurate.

keyTerms.meaning: A mourner (here: the laws of mourning)

phrases.english: Like Rabbi Shimon regarding a mourner, what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the טרפה half to the אבל half of the report
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the הלכה follows רבי שמעון in the case of the late-arriving mourner

steps.title: It is a dispute among the אמוראים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא says this is disputed. רב חסדא and רבי יוחנן say the הלכה follows רבי שמעון, and רב נחמן says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is a dispute, as it was stated: רב חסדא says it is the הלכה, and so says רבי יוחנן, it is the הלכה. רב נחמן says it is not the הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא doesn't give one clear answer. He reports that אמוראים disagree about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the report about רבי יוחנן is confirmed: he does rule like רבי שמעון. But רב נחמן disagrees, so the question is still open until the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute, a difference of opinion
They are
And similarly, and the same

phrases.english: He said to him: It is a dispute,
as it was stated:
Rav Ḥisda says it is the halakha,
and so says Rabbi Yoḥanan: it is the halakha,
and Rav Naḥman says it is not the halakha.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The matter is disputed: רב חסדא and רבי יוחנן rule like רבי שמעון, and רב נחמן does not.

steps.title: Final ruling on טרפה and on mourning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on טרפה, but is like רבי שמעון on אבל, because שמואל said that in mourning we follow the lenient view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is not like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל regarding טרפה, and the הלכה is like רבי שמעון regarding mourning, as שמואל said: the הלכה follows the lenient view in mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling on both questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On טרפה, רבי אבא's correction stands: לֵיחָה does not seal the hole. On אבל, the dispute from the previous step is settled by שמואל's general rule. רבי שמעון is the lenient view, so we follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: In mourning laws, the הלכה follows the more lenient opinion
The one who rules leniently

steps.whatToRemember: Final rulings: (1) לֵיחָה sealing a hole in the intestines does not help, and the animal is a טרפה. (2) A mourner from nearby can join the family's count even on the seventh day, like רבי שמעון, because in אבל we follow the lenient view.
steps.whyThisMatters: שמואל's rule, הלכה כדברי המיקל באבל, is a general principle. It settles many disputes about mourning laws, not just this one.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בִּטְרֵפָה,
phrases.english: And the halakha is not like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel regarding a tereifa,
and the halakha is like Rabbi Shimon regarding mourning,
as Shmuel said:
The halakha follows the words of the lenient one in mourning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בִּטְרֵפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the dispute of step 18 and confirms the correction of step 16
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: No הלכה like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on טרפה. The הלכה follows רבי שמעון on אבל, based on שמואל's rule to follow the lenient view in mourning.

steps.title: We may compare holes in the intestines
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר חייא rules that we may compare a doubtful hole in the בני מעיים with a new hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר חייא said: We may compare holes in the intestines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. רב שימי בר חייא gives a way to check a hole in the intestines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we don't know whether a hole came before or after שחיטה, we make a new hole and compare the two. If they look the same, the first hole is also new, so the animal is not a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: We compare (make a new hole and set it next to the old one)
Intestines

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya said:
We may compare holes in the intestines.
phrases.notes: He means: make a fresh hole and see if it looks like the doubtful one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic after the conclusion about טרפה and אבל in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doubtful hole in the intestines may be checked by comparing it to a new hole.

steps.title: רבא's comparison fails, but his son's works
steps.stepSummary: Intestines came before רבא. His comparison did not match, but his son רב משרשיא rubbed the new holes and they matched.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some intestines came before רבא. He compared the holes, and they did not look alike. His son רב משרשיא came, rubbed the new holes, and then they looked alike.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case where the comparing method from step 20 was used. This story sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the new hole and the old hole looked different, which would make the animal a טרפה. רב משרשיא rubbed the new hole, and then it matched the old one.

keyTerms.meaning: They looked alike
Rubbing, handling with the hand

phrases.english: There were certain intestines
that came before Rava.
He compared them, and they did not look alike.
Rav Mesharshiyya, his son, came,
rubbed them, and they looked alike.
phrases.notes: He rubbed the new holes, so they would look handled like the old one.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ בְּנֵי מֵעַיִים דַּאֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that applies the rule of step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The new hole should be rubbed before it is compared with the old one.

steps.title: רבא asks his son how he knew
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב משרשיא where he got the idea to rub the holes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Where did you get this from?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks his son to explain why he rubbed the holes. This sets up the son's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rubbing changed the result, so רבא wants to know the reason behind it. This is a real question, not an attack.

keyTerms.meaning: Where do you get this from?

phrases.english: He said to him: Where do you get this from?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the son's action in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for rubbing the new holes before comparing.

steps.title: The old holes had already been handled
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא explains that many hands touched the old holes before they reached רבא, so the new ones must be handled too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: How many hands rubbed these before they came before the master!
steps.whatsHappening: The son explains his reasoning. The old holes were touched by many people, so a fair comparison needs the new holes touched too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Handling changes how a hole looks. A clean new hole would never match a hole that many people had handled, so you must make them equal before you compare.

keyTerms.meaning: How many hands
Master (a respectful way of saying 'you')

phrases.english: He said to him:
How many hands rubbed these
before they came before the master!
phrases.notes: He is speaking to his father רבא, calling him 'master' out of respect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The old holes were handled by many people, so the new holes must be handled too before comparing.

steps.title: רבא praises his son
steps.stepSummary: רבא says his son is as wise in טרפות as רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: My son is as wise in טרפות as רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא accepts his son's reasoning and praises him. This closes the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The praise shows that rubbing before comparing is accepted. The story adds a practical detail to the rule of step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: Wise
Defects that make an animal not kosher

steps.whatToRemember: When comparing holes, first rub the new hole so it is in the same state as the old, handled hole.

phrases.english: He said to him:
My son is as wise in tereifot as Rabbi Yoḥanan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer of step 23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Rubbing the new hole before comparing is the correct method.

steps.title: We may compare holes in the lung
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר both rule that the comparing method also works for the ריאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר both say: We may compare holes in the lung.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the same comparing method, now for the lung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method from the intestines is applied to a second organ. A doubtful hole in the lung can be checked against a new hole.

keyTerms.meaning: Lung
Both of them

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Elazar
who both say:
We may compare holes in the lung.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the comparing rule to another organ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Holes in the lung may be checked by comparing.

steps.title: רבא limits lung comparison to the same section
steps.stepSummary: רבא says you may compare only within the same section of the lung, not from one section to another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We said this only within the same section. But from one section to another, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a limit to the rule of step 25.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Different parts of the lung may look different. So רבא says the new hole must be made in the same section as the old hole.

keyTerms.meaning: We said this only...
Section or side of the lung (literally 'garden bed')

phrases.english: Rava said:
We said this only within the same section,
but from one section to another section, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule of step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lung comparison is allowed only within the same section.

steps.title: The הלכה for the lung
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה allows comparing even between sections, and between animals of the same size, but not between a large and a small animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: even from section to section, from small to small, and from large to large. But not from large to small, and not from small to large.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling and does not follow רבא's limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Section does not matter, but the size of the animal does. A small animal's lung may be compared only to a small one, and a large one only to a large one.

keyTerms.meaning: And the final ruling is
Small animal (like sheep or goats)
Large animal (like cattle)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix the two limits. The section limit of רבא is rejected, but the size limit is the הלכה.

phrases.english: And the halakha is:
even from one section to another section,
from a small animal to a small one, and from a large animal to a large one,
phrases.notes: So you may even compare with a new hole made in another animal of the same size.

phrases.english: but not from a large animal to a small one,
and not from a small animal to a large one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules against the limit of step 26.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Lung holes may be compared across sections and between animals of the same size, but not between a large and a small animal.

steps.title: We may compare holes in the windpipe
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא both rule that the comparing method also works for the קנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both say: We may compare holes in the windpipe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the comparing method to a third body part, the windpipe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the lung: first a rule, then a limit, then the final הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Windpipe

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava, who both say:
We may compare holes in the windpipe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the comparing rule to another body part.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Holes in the windpipe may be checked by comparing.

steps.title: רב פפא limits windpipe comparison to the same ring
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says you may compare only within the same ring of the windpipe.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: We said this only within the same ring. But from one ring to another, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a limit to the rule of step 28, just like רבא did for the lung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each ring of the windpipe may look different. So רב פפא wants the new hole made in the same ring as the old one.

keyTerms.meaning: A ring (segment) of the windpipe

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
We said this only within the same ring,
but from one ring to another ring, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule of step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Windpipe comparison is allowed only within the same ring.

steps.title: The הלכה for the windpipe
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה allows comparing ring to ring and small ring to small ring, but not a ring to a small ring.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: even from ring to ring, and from small ring to small ring. But not from a ring to a small ring, and not from a small ring to a ring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling for the windpipe and does not follow רב פפא's limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is the type of ring, not whether it is the same one. A main ring may be compared with any main ring, and a small in-between ring with any small ring, but the two types may not be mixed.

keyTerms.meaning: A small in-between ring of the windpipe

steps.whatToRemember: In all three body parts we may compare holes. The comparison must be between things of the same kind: the same size of animal for the lung, and the same type of ring for the windpipe.

phrases.english: And the halakha is:
even from one ring to another ring,
and from a small ring to another small ring,
phrases.notes: These are the thin rings that sit between the main rings.

phrases.english: but not from a ring to a small ring,
and not from a small ring to a ring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules against the limit of step 29.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Windpipe holes may be compared between rings of the same type, but not between a main ring and a small ring.

steps.title: זעירי: a hole in the rectum is kosher
steps.stepSummary: זעירי rules that an animal whose rectum was punctured is כשרה, because the hips hold the rectum in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי said: If the rectum was punctured, the animal is kosher, because the hips hold it in place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. זעירי gives a ruling about a hole in the חלחולת (the last part of the intestine, the rectum).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a hole in an inner organ can make an animal a טרפה. זעירי says this hole does not, because the hip area holds the rectum firmly and closes off the hole. His reason is about support from outside, not about the hole being too small to matter.

keyTerms.meaning: The rectum, the end part of the intestine
That was punctured, that has a hole in it
The hips or thighs of the animal
Hold up, hold firmly in place

phrases.english: Ze'eiri said: A rectum that was punctured
is kosher, since the hips hold it in place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of comparing lungs and windpipe rings (steps 25-30).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A punctured rectum does not make the animal a טרפה, because the hips hold it and seal the hole.

steps.title: How much of the rectum does this cover?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how far זעירי's rule reaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to pin down the limits of זעירי's rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זעירי's reason is that the hips hold the rectum. So the גמרא wants to know which part of the rectum, and how big a hole, this reason really covers. The question challenges nothing. It only asks for the exact limits.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much? It asks for the size or extent of a rule

phrases.english: And how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the limits of זעירי's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The extent of the rectum, and the size of the hole, that זעירי's kosher ruling covers.

steps.title: Where it is attached, even most of it; elsewhere, any hole
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעי in the name of רבי יוחנן: at the place where the rectum is attached to the hips, even a hole through most of it is kosher. Away from there, any hole at all makes it a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: In the place where it is attached, even if most of it is holed, it is kosher. Not in the place where it is attached, even the smallest hole makes it a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Where the rectum is attached to the hips, the rule is very lenient. Where it is not attached, the rule is very strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows זעירי's reason exactly. Where the hips actually hold the rectum, they seal even a big hole, up to most of its width. Where there is no attachment, nothing seals the hole, so even a tiny one makes the animal a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where the rectum is attached to the hips
In most of it, a hole through the majority
With any amount at all, even the smallest hole

steps.whatToRemember: The rectum is lenient only where it is attached to the hips (kosher even if most of it is holed). Away from the attachment, any hole makes it a טרפה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'בְּרוּבּוֹ' as the point where it becomes a טרפה. It is the opposite: at the attached spot it is kosher even with a hole through most of it. 'בְּמַשֶּׁהוּ' means any small hole makes it a טרפה where it is not attached.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעַי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ilai said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
In the place where it is attached, even through most of it,
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves out the word 'kosher'. He means it stays kosher even with a hole that big.

phrases.english: not in the place where it is attached, with any amount.
phrases.notes: Here he means the animal becomes a טרפה with even the tiniest hole.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעַי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מְקוֹם הַדֶּבֶק בְּרוּבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question 'וכמה' from step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: At the attached spot, a hole through most of the rectum is kosher. Away from it, any hole makes the animal a טרפה.

steps.title: רבא objects to linking the ruling to רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים repeated this ruling before רבא in the name of רב נחמן. רבא protested that he had told them not to hang things on רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים said this ruling before רבא in the name of רב נחמן. רבא said: Didn't I tell you not to hang on him...
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים repeat this ruling to רבא but say it comes from רב נחמן. רבא objects. His sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא objects when the ruling is said in רב נחמן's name. He reminds them that he had warned them not to 'hang' things on רב נחמן. His sentence, and the reason for his objection, continue on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him, in his presence
In his name, quoting him as the source
Don't hang on him, meaning don't attach sayings to him

phrases.english: The Sages said it before Rava
in the name of Rav Nachman. He said:
Didn't I tell you
not to hang on him

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמְרוּהָ רַבָּנַן קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports how this ruling was quoted before רבא and his objection to the name it was said in.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the ruling comes from רב נחמן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא had already warned them not to attach sayings to רב נחמן. His full reason continues on the next amud.
